bull_thesis_sentence: Broadcom is the only company that simultaneously designs the custom silicon and the Ethernet fabric powering hyperscaler AI clusters, a dual-franchise position that drives more than $100bn of guided FY27 AI semiconductor revenue at 67%+ EBITDA margins, while the VMware software annuity compounds cash flow through the semiconductor cycle.
bull_thesis_bullets: Six signed hyperscaler XPU programs (Google, Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI + two unnamed) underwrite management's FY27 AI revenue guide of >$100bn across ~10GW of datacenter deployments, supported by $73bn of 18-month backlog (Dec 2025) and multi-year supply agreements through 2029-2031; AI semiconductor revenue has accelerated every quarter — Q1-FY26 +106%, Q2-FY26 +143% YoY to $10.8bn, Q3-FY26 guided ~$16bn (+~200% YoY).

Networking is the more durable, vendor-agnostic half of the AI franchise: Tomahawk 6 leads merchant Ethernet switching at 51.2 Tbps, SerDes at 1.6+ Tb/s is the backbone of scale-up clusters, and AI networking contributed ~40% of Q2-FY26 AI semiconductor revenue — a socket that does not disappear if a hyperscaler co-designs its own XPU.

At $376.71, the stock trades at 19.5x forward non-GAAP EPS of $19.35 (FY26E) and ~17.6x on FY27E EPS of $21.40, for a franchise generating $27bn of free cash flow (42-46% FCF margin) with 45 analysts at a mean target of $522 and net debt falling toward zero by FY27; the post-Q2 drawdown of ~22% from the June 2 ATH of $481.57 resets the entry without any change in the demand signal.

bull_catalysts.title: Q3-FY26 AI revenue proof point — the 2H26 doubling (Sep 2026)
bull_catalysts.body: Broadcom guided Q3-FY26 total revenue of $29.4bn (+84% YoY) with AI semiconductors at ~$16bn, implying ~100% half-on-half AI growth in 2H26. A Q3 AI print at or above $16bn — against the quarterly pattern of consistently beating guidance (Q2: guided ~$10.x bn, printed $10.8bn; Q1: guided $8.2bn, printed $8.4bn; Q4-FY25: guided $6.2bn, printed $6.5bn) — refutes the 'no guide-up = ceiling' bear narrative and likely re-rates the stock toward the $485-525 Street target. Adjusted EBITDA margin was guided at 68%, above the Q2 actual of 67.3%, making this release simultaneously a volume, margin, and management-credibility event. Source: Q2-FY26 8-K (SEC, 3 Jun 2026); GS 3 Jun 2026 (Drive).

bull_catalysts.title: Google + Anthropic multi-generation supply agreement through 2031
bull_catalysts.body: On April 6, 2026, Broadcom filed an 8-K disclosing a Long Term Agreement with Google for future TPU generations and a Supply Assurance Agreement covering networking and rack components through 2031. Separately, Broadcom, Google, and Anthropic expanded their collaboration: Anthropic will access at least 3.5GW of TPU-based AI compute starting in FY27, scaling toward 5GW. Goldman Sachs estimates Google and Anthropic combined will represent ~70% of Broadcom's AI XPU revenues in FY27-28, contributing $64.5bn-$75.7bn of the guided >$100bn. The 2031 commitment covers six or more silicon generations and locks in Broadcom's networking position even if hyperscalers internalize more physical design over time. Source: Broadcom 8-K Apr 2026; GS 7 Apr 2026 (Drive).

bull_catalysts.title: Meta MTIA partnership — 1GW initial, 3GW through FY28
bull_catalysts.body: On April 14, 2026, Broadcom announced a multi-year, multi-generation strategic partnership with Meta covering Meta's MTIA custom compute chips, with supply chain commitments extending through 2029. The initial phase exceeds 1GW, with a sustained multi-gigawatt rollout guided to reach 3GW shipped through FY28. The partnership includes both XPU supply and networking solutions (scale-up, scale-out, and scale-across), making it a full-stack AI infrastructure relationship. CEO Hock Tan joined Meta's board advisory role for custom silicon direction, deepening the engineering lock-in. This removes one of the market's prior concerns that Meta was diversifying away from Broadcom. Source: Broadcom press release Apr 14, 2026; GS 14 Apr 2026 (Drive).

bull_catalysts.title: OpenAI and two unnamed XPU customers begin shipping in late 2026
bull_catalysts.body: Broadcom is engaged with OpenAI to deliver initial custom XPU product in FY26, deploying 1.3GW in FY27. Two additional unnamed XPU customers are expected to begin shipping in late 2026, with $6bn of purchase orders already secured. These engagements represent new revenue legs not yet in the run-rate, broadening the customer base from three to six and reducing single-customer concentration risk. Each XPU program is co-designed over 18-24 months and spans multiple silicon generations, creating high switching costs. The pipeline converts abstract 'SAM' into contracted backlog with signed POs. Source: GS 3 Jun 2026 (Drive); Q2-FY26 8-K (SEC).

bull_catalysts.title: AI networking moat — Tomahawk 7 ramp in FY26-27
bull_catalysts.body: Broadcom's Ethernet switching (Tomahawk 6 shipping, Tomahawk 7 in development) and SerDes leadership at 1.6+ Tb/s are the connective tissue for AI scale-out clusters. Networking contributed ~40% of Q2-FY26 AI semiconductor revenue and is expected to revert toward 30-40% long-term. This franchise is structurally more defensible than the XPU design-service business: even customers pursuing Customer-Owned-Tooling (COT) strategies still need best-in-class Ethernet fabric. Tomahawk's merchant position means it sells into Nvidia, AMD, and custom-silicon clusters alike, giving Broadcom a second, vendor-agnostic way to capture AI infrastructure capex. Source: Q2-FY26 8-K; GS 3 Jun 2026 (Drive); UBS 3 Jun 2026 (Drive).

bull_catalysts.title: VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 renewal wave — software guided +31% YoY in Q3-FY26
bull_catalysts.body: Infrastructure Software segment grew +9% YoY in Q2-FY26 and is guided +31% YoY in Q3-FY26, driven by the VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) 9.1 release and the multi-year bridge contract renewals entering the active window. Broadcom reports 87% of its top-10,000 customers renew with VCF, and management cited increasing core count deployment across Nvidia, Intel, and AMD-based systems driving on-premise VM uptick. Software runs at ~70s EBITDA margin; at 42% of FY25 revenue, it contributes a high-quality recurring cash stream that smooths the semiconductor cycle. The VCF 9.1 cycle beginning in Q3-FY26 is the first material upside catalyst for the software segment since the VMware repricing was complete. Source: Q2-FY26 8-K (SEC); GS 3 Jun 2026 (Drive).

bull_catalysts.title: Fortress FCF compounding toward $40bn+ — rapid de-levering
bull_catalysts.body: Broadcom generated FY25 free cash flow of $26.9bn (42% of revenue) and Q2-FY26 FCF of $10.3bn (46% of quarterly revenue) — the highest quarterly FCF in company history. The fabless model keeps capex at ~1% of sales ($623mn in FY25). Net debt was ~$46bn at Q2-FY26 (net debt/EBITDA ~1.1-1.3x in FY25); management guides to ~0.4x in FY26E and net cash by FY27E as the FCF compounds. The company returned $11.1bn via dividends and $2.45bn via buybacks in FY25 and authorized a new $10bn buyback in March 2026. FY26 dividend is $2.60/share (15th consecutive annual increase). A $2.5bn notes tender was launched in June 2026. FCF per share is rising as AI mix expands. Source: FY2025 10-K (SEC); Q2-FY26 8-K; GS 3 Jun 2026 (Drive).

bull_catalysts.title: Consistent beat-and-raise track record across 5 consecutive quarters
bull_catalysts.body: Revenue guidance vs. actual: Q2-FY25 guided ~$14.9bn / printed $15.0bn; Q3-FY25 ~$15.8bn / $15.95bn; Q4-FY25 ~$17.4bn / $18.0bn; Q1-FY26 ~$19.1bn / $19.3bn; Q2-FY26 ~$22.0bn / $22.2bn. AI semiconductor revenue has beaten guidance in each quarter: Q4-FY25 $6.2bn guided / $6.5bn actual; Q1-FY26 $8.2bn / $8.4bn; Q2-FY26 ~$10.x bn / $10.8bn. The pattern reflects management's discipline of conservative guidance and operational execution. CEO Hock Tan and CFO Kirsten Spears have driven revenue from $35.8bn (FY23) to $63.9bn (FY25) to a FY26E run-rate above $100bn, each year delivering against or above plan. Source: Broadcom 8-K filings (SEC EDGAR CIK 0001730168); Stage 6 moat audit (Drive, 15 Jun 2026).

bull_catalysts.title: Supply chain secured through FY27 — inventory pre-build confirms demand
bull_catalysts.body: Management disclosed it has secured all key components — memory, lasers, packaging, substrates — needed to support its revenue forecast through FY27, and is currently working to secure FY28 supply. Inventory grew from $3.0bn (Q1-FY26) to $4.3bn (Q2-FY26) ahead of the 2H26 AI doubling, consistent with a demand-driven pre-build rather than a speculative overstock. Supply constraints were cited as the primary reason Q2 AI revenue came in at $10.8bn vs. a higher demand level, making supply assurance the key FY26H2 upside enabler. The Apollo/Blackstone $35bn AI XPV vehicle (June 9, 2026) provides additional off-balance-sheet financing for AI infrastructure buildout by Broadcom's hyperscaler customers, extending the capex runway. Source: Q2-FY26 8-K; GS 3 Jun 2026 (Drive); UBS 3 Jun 2026 (Drive).

bull_catalysts.title: Valuation reset — 22% drawdown with no demand deterioration
bull_catalysts.body: AVGO closed at an all-time high of $481.57 on June 2, 2026, then fell 12.6% on June 4 (market reaction to 'no guide-up') and has declined a further ~4% to $376.71. The drawdown is entirely a multiple compression event — the 2H26 AI guide of ~$56bn for FY26 and the >$100bn FY27 AI commitment were unchanged. The forward P/E compressed from ~42x at the ATH to ~19.5x on FY26 EPS of $19.35. Goldman Sachs raised its price target from $500 to $525 on June 3, 2026 (30x normalized EPS of $17.50); UBS maintains $485. The Street mean is $522.06, median $525, from 45 analysts with a recommendation mean of 1.33 (strong buy). The risk/reward at current levels — 19.5x on a franchise growing AI revenue at 100%+ — is materially better than at the prior ATH. Source: Macrotrends; GS 3 Jun 2026 (Drive); yfinance (17 Jun 2026).

business_facts.summary: Broadcom Inc. is a fabless semiconductor and infrastructure-software company with two segments: Semiconductor Solutions (~58% of FY25 revenue), which designs custom AI accelerators (XPUs/ASICs), AI/Ethernet networking (Tomahawk switches, Jericho routers, SerDes), and a diversified non-AI franchise (broadband, wireless, server storage, industrial); and Infrastructure Software (~42% of FY25 revenue), centered on VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) sold as a recurring subscription, plus CA mainframe and Symantec enterprise security. FY25 revenue was $63.9bn; FY26E is ~$107bn (GS). The stock trades on NASDAQ under AVGO.
business_facts.business_model: Semiconductor Solutions earns per-unit revenue from silicon designed at Broadcom but fabricated by TSMC (fabless), with zero direct manufacturing capex. AI XPU programs are co-designed with hyperscaler customers over 18-24 months and span multiple silicon generations. Infrastructure Software generates recurring annual subscription fees through VCF and bundled enterprise software; Broadcom collapsed VMware's ~600 SKUs into a handful of bundles and moved customers onto multi-year contracts. Blended non-GAAP gross margin was ~77% in Q2-FY26; adjusted EBITDA margin was 67.3% in Q2-FY26.

AI semiconductor revenue: Q2-FY26 $10.8bn (+143% YoY), Q3-FY26 guided ~$16bn. Company-level non-GAAP gross margin 77.1% in Q2-FY26. Segment-level margins not disclosed separately by company; estimated ~75-80% gross margin based on AI silicon pricing.

industry_position_bull.market_overview: Custom AI ASIC market is projected to grow ~45% in 2026 (vs ~16% for merchant GPUs) and toward ~$118bn by 2033 (TrendForce/TheNextWeb). The structural driver is hyperscaler dissatisfaction with merchant GPU margins and thermal/performance constraints — hyperscalers want silicon purpose-built for their workloads. Broadcom holds ~60-70% of this custom-accelerator market. AI Ethernet networking (scale-out fabric) grows with cluster size and is not subject to the same commoditization pressure as merchant silicon. The company is in its third year of accelerating AI revenue growth; management guides >$100bn in FY27 AI semiconductor revenue — more than the entire company's revenue in FY24 ($51.6bn).
industry_position_bull.moat: The XPU moat is switching cost and co-design lock-in: a hyperscaler XPU is co-engineered over 18-24 months and tied to the customer's software stack; re-architecting to a new silicon vendor takes years. The networking moat is architectural leadership (Tomahawk 6/7, Jericho3-AI, SerDes) combined with vendor agnosticism — Broadcom wins the fabric whether the customer buys Nvidia, AMD, or custom silicon. VMware creates enterprise lock-in through hypervisor API dependencies, management tooling (vCenter), and the cost of workload migration. None of the three moat legs is easily displaced on a one-to-three-year horizon.

peers_positive_read: Against Nvidia (forward P/E ~30x+, pure hardware, no software annuity), Broadcom's 19.5x forward multiple looks undemanding for a company with comparable AI revenue growth, higher EBITDA margins (67% vs Nvidia's ~60%), and a 42% recurring software base that dampens cyclicality. Marvell, the closest custom-silicon comp, is at a fraction of Broadcom's scale, has no software cushion, and trades at a higher revenue multiple. Intel has no credible custom-silicon franchise. The peer set frames Broadcom as the cash-compounding, software-de-risked way to own AI infrastructure — not the highest-beta AI play, but the one with the widest moat and the most attractive risk-adjusted return at current prices.

bull_valuation_lens.method_reasoning: Broadcom is two materially different businesses: a high-growth AI-led semiconductor franchise that deserves a DCF capturing the steep but decaying FCF ramp, and a recurring-revenue enterprise software annuity (VMware) that the market pays an EV/EBITDA multiple for. A single blended multiple understates the software half and obscures the AI silicon optionality. SOTP with a DCF on semiconductors and an EV/EBITDA on software is the honest frame, consistent with how GS and UBS model the stock internally.

bull_dcf_assumptions.wacc_reasoning: 8.2% blends a 4.3% risk-free rate, 1.30 beta (below the reported 1.43 because the software annuity lowers aggregate cash-flow volatility), 4.5% ERP, and a small after-tax debt weight on an investment-grade balance sheet de-levering toward net cash.
bull_dcf_assumptions.terminal_growth_reasoning: 4.3% for the semiconductor segment reflects durable AI-content growth above nominal GDP as cluster scale compounds, decaying from the explicit AI ramp but staying above a mature-semis 3% terminal rate.
bull_dcf_assumptions.fcf_growth_reasoning: Semiconductor segment FCF growing from ~$30bn in FY26 toward ~$80bn by FY32 as the XPU ramp (Google, Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI + 2 more) and Tomahawk/SerDes networking scale into the >$100bn FY27 AI revenue guide. Software segment valued separately at 17x EV/EBITDA on ~$19bn software EBITDA.

bull_software_multiple.reasoning: 18x forward EV/EBITDA for the VMware segment — at a premium to legacy enterprise software for the 70s operating margin and the multi-year contract lock-in, below high-growth SaaS because net retention is 'price-up beats footprint-down' rather than organic expansion. VCF 9.1 and the Q3-FY26 +31% guide support a modest re-rate vs the prior 17x base.
